What comes next: science, social studies, and language arts

The four Math levels are done. This page tells you how the other three GED subjects will be organized, so you can comment before the lessons are written. Each subject already has a public page with its full plan (in English and in Spanish); the buttons below open them.

Science · plan Social studies · plan Language arts · plan

2. What stays the same as in Math

  • Lesson and practice page. Each lesson has its own practice page with activities that make new exercises every time, linked by section.
  • Two tries. First wrong answer: a hint. Second: the solution, explained. Two-choice questions explain right away.
  • English and Spanish. Both versions are built from the same source, so they teach exactly the same thing.
  • GED and CCR standards at the end of each lesson, taken from the official GED Assessment Guide.
  • Accessible. Keyboard navigation, text descriptions for every figure, larger text and high contrast, and nothing to install.
  • Everything on LearnGED. No accounts, no outside sites: the readings, the tools, and the practice live here.
↑ Back to top

3. Order of work

  1. Science first: it already exists in Spanish (24 lessons), so it follows the same path as Math, lesson by lesson, in both languages at once.
  2. Social studies next: it also exists in Spanish (24 lessons and a source archive of real documents).
  3. Reasoning through language arts last: the Spanish path comes from GEDparaHispanos, but the English path is a new course and needs your help the most.
↑ Back to top

4. Questions for you

  1. Units in science. Math uses US customary units only. Science, like the GED Science test, uses metric units (grams, meters, liters, °C). We plan to use metric units in science and give the US equivalent the first time each unit appears. Does that match what your students need?
  2. Science by area, not by level. Is it useful for your students to choose an area (life, physical, Earth and space) after the two skills topics, or would you rather have a single fixed order?
  3. Social studies documents. The English version will link each primary source to the official transcript (National Archives, Library of Congress, and others). Are there documents you always use that we should add?
  4. State constitution. Lesson 8.3 of Social studies includes the Illinois Constitution, which some Illinois programs require. Should it stay, or become an optional page?
  5. Reading and writing in English. Please look at the outline of the four levels on the language arts plan. What is missing for your students? What would you move to another level?
  6. Texts. Which public-domain authors or kinds of texts (workplace documents, news, letters, speeches) work best with your students?
  7. Would you like to help write or review one of these subjects? Tell us which one.
↑ Back to top

5. How to send comments

Any format is fine: an email or a list. Please say which subject and, if you can, which topic or lesson. Send your comments to José M. Fernández (Zhema).
